summary_en: A multicenter clinical study combining dermoscopic guidance with portable 33 MHz high-frequency ultrasound to characterize basal cell carcinoma subtypes non-invasively. Across 87 histologically confirmed lesions, the study identifies subtype-associated ultrasound features, including ribbon-like morphology for superficial BCC, oval shape and hyperechoic spots for nodular BCC, and acoustic shadowing for infiltrative BCC. It is relevant as an optical-guided acoustic imaging application, but does not introduce a new reconstruction or sensing method.
